title: An AI radio DJ has shot to stardom in L.A. Human hosts aren’t happy about it
key_facts: José FM, a Spanish-language station in Los Angeles owned by Entravision, pairs human DJ Geraldine Guzman (DJ GeeGee) with an AI co-host called Coyotec.
Coyotec's voice was built with ElevenLabs technology from the voice of Entravision Audio president Eduardo Maytorena; the character has aired live since May.
The show moved from once a week on weekends to weekday commuting hours and is now also broadcast in English and in cities including Sacramento, Las Vegas and El Paso.
The station says the show brought a surge of Latino male listeners aged 25 to 54, but it is unclear whether that is due to GeeGee, Coyotec or both.
SAG-AFTRA, which represents radio personalities, says replacing humans with synthetic substitutes deceives audiences and undermines livelihoods.
Bureau of Labor Statistics figures cited: radio broadcasting jobs fell from 85,000 in 2019 to 66,000 in 2025, about 22%.

Maytorena says the AI host is not about saving money, since developing and running it cost more than some human hosts; its main value is live ad pitches ('for every dollar I spend, if I'm able to generate $10').
Other stations use AI hosts too; iHeartMedia runs a 'Guaranteed Human' campaign against synthetic hosts, and critic Sam Gregory warns people may come to trust a predictive text machine.
quote_evidence: Listeners of L.A.’s José FM are repeatedly told they are listening to AI but seem to like it.
The station says the AI-co-hosted show sparked a surge in Latino male listeners ages 25 to 54.
It is unclear whether the uptick was because of GeeGee, Coyotec or both.
why_it_matters_hint: AI hosts are moving from experiments to prime-time radio shows, raising questions about jobs and about listeners trusting a voice that has no real stake in what it says.
event_date: Ongoing; Coyotec has aired live since May 2026; LA Times feature published 2 Oct 2026
notes: Single-outlet feature; the audience gains are the station's own claim, and the article says the cause is unclear. Feature about an ongoing trend, so marked NEW as a report, not a follow-up.
